ds RNA from killer strains and from nonkiller strains of yeast, as well as from a nonkiller strain that lacks all dsRNA, hybridize with DNA of yeast.

ds RNA of the yeast S. cerevisiae hybridizes with the nuclear DNA of the same yeast, that this hybridization occurs with DNA from all the strains tested, and that the extent of hybridization is the same regardless of the strains of origin of the ds RNA and the DNA.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
killer ds RNA and nuclear DNA are not homologous.

ds RNA is homologous to DNA in the host cell, but the extent of homology is low.
